preconditions.description: The input string E is a valid Ahmes arithmetic expression with erased operators (represented as '?'), and its length is between 1 and 10^4 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: P >= 0 and M >= 0 and P + M == E.count('?')
preconditions.description: P and M are non-negative integers representing the number of plus and minus operators, respectively, and their sum equals the total number of erased operators ('?') in E.

preconditions.expression: all(c in '()123456789?' for c in E)
preconditions.description: The string E consists only of digits (1-9), parentheses '(', ')', and erased operators '?'.
The parentheses in E are balanced.

postconditions.description: The output is a single line containing the maximum possible value of the Ahmes arithmetic expression E after replacing exactly P '+' and M '-' operators in place of the '?' characters.

postconditions.expression: all(op in '+-' for op in operators) and operators.count('+') == P and operators.count('-') == M
postconditions.description: The operators used to replace '?' in E are exactly P '+' and M '-', and the expression is evaluated with these operators to produce the maximum possible value.

postconditions.expression: max_value == max(evaluate(E.replace('?', op, count)) for op in ['+', '-'] for count in combinations_with_replacement('+-', P, M))
postconditions.description: The output is the maximum value achievable by replacing the '?' in E with any combination of P '+' and M '-' operators, where combinations_with_replacement is a helper representing all possible operator assignments.
